Essex County honors Latino leaders at annual heritage month celebration
Essex County honored Assemblywoman Carmen Morales and retired Judge Jose L. Linares during its annual Latino Heritage Month Celebration on Oct. 8 in Newark. The event recognized their leadership contributions while celebrating local Latino culture.
Essex County Executive Joseph N. DiVincenzo, Jr. hosted the county’s Annual Latino Heritage Celebration on Oct. 8 at the Essex County Martin Luther King, Jr. Justice Building in Newark to honor residents with roots in Spanish-speaking nations of Europe, Central America, South America, and the Caribbean.
During the event, DiVincenzo presented the 2026 Estrella del Condado de Essex Awards (Stars of Essex County) to New Jersey Assemblywoman Carmen Morales and retired Chief Judge Jose L. Linares for their leadership and dedication to public service. “We are proud to recognize Carmen Morales and Jose Linares for their outstanding leadership, dedication to public service, and commitment to improving the lives of all our residents,” DiVincenzo said. “Our cultural celebrations not only honor the diversity of Essex County but also give us the opportunity to learn from and celebrate the rich heritage of our constituents,” he added.
Morales is an education leader representing New Jersey’s 34th Legislative District as Assemblywoman and serves as Director of Curriculum and Instruction for Essex County Schools of Technology. She began her career teaching preschool in Newark before advancing through various educational roles over two decades. As a first-generation college student who grew up in public housing, Morales emphasized family involvement and mentorship for students throughout her career. She currently chairs the assembly Higher Education committee and is a member of several others focused on science, technology, appropriations, community growth, and women’s empowerment.
“To my students from the Vocational School District, you keep me hopeful for the future, you keep me growing and reminding me of why what we do is important. My desire to give back is a culmination of my family, my upbringing and my experiences in life,” said Morales.
Judge Linares served as Chief Judge of the U.S. District Court in New Jersey after being nominated by the President in 2002; he was previously a Superior Court Judge in Essex County as well as head of his own law firm specializing in litigation cases involving products liability or medical issues. He has extensive experience with patent cases—particularly those involving disputes between generic drug companies—and has presided over major bankruptcy appeals, class actions, multidistrict litigations, and securities fraud cases during his judicial tenure.
“I am proud of my accomplishments as a judge, but I am most proud of my family and the sacrifices made by my parents. As Latinos we are instilled with a large amount of pride, family, religion, values and work ethic that is unparalleled,” Linares said.
The celebration included an invocation by Pastor Madalyn Santos from Newark Community Church along with musical entertainment provided by Arts High School's Latin Jazz Band. The Latino Heritage Month Celebration forms part of a year-long series highlighting cultural diversity within Essex County.
